The DRAW arrows answer to 1, 2, 3

The DRAW group named three protocols and offered no way to reach any of them but the mouse. Each button now carries its digit, says it out loud to a screen reader, and repeats it in the tooltip — and the keys work, from the engine's own shortcut layer, so they behave like every other shortcut in the app including staying quiet while you are typing a name.

Three protocols, three digits

The mapping is the order the bar paints them, which is the only mapping that needs no legend — and the reason the digit has to be visible on the button rather than hidden in a tooltip. Their initials were not available: S is already the Simple card face and A is already the Arrow group.

↝Stream1

Pub/sub: publisher → subscriber

SService2

Client → server; request and response

AAction3

Client → server; goal, feedback and result

The digits were not free

Stock tldraw already spends 10 digits — 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 0 — on activate the nth toolbar tool (NUMBERED_SHORTCUT_KEYS in OverflowingToolbar, tldraw 5.3.2). It listens on the container document; the shortcut layer that runs our action listens on body. Body runs first. So the first attempt looked like the key doing nothing at all: pressing 2 armed Service and was undone, in the same keystroke, by a synthetic click on the Cursor button. The trace is what found it — the second setCurrentTool came from onClick on systemsketch-tool-cursor, with isTrusted: false.

That is why this is a loan rather than a seizure. The claim is exactly as narrow as the group that explains it: three digits, no modifiers, only while the communication lens is open on an Async region (shouldClaimCommunicationDigit, communicationDrawShortcuts.ts:90). Everywhere else in SystemSketch, 1–9 still pick toolbar tools.

Every state, from the real app

Evidence

12unit checks on the digit map, the arming, and the precedence rule
7real-browser checks in npm run test:draw-hotkeys
0console errors across the journey

In the browser

  • each DRAW button paints its digit, announces it, and names it in the tooltip — left to right, 1 2 3
  • 1, 2 and 3 each arm their own protocol, and swap directly between them while armed
  • pressing the armed digit again disarms it, exactly as clicking the pressed button does
  • a relationship drawn after pressing 2 generates the same canonical Service legs the button does
  • a digit pressed while a text field has focus types, and arms nothing
  • no console errors across the whole journey
  • outside the group the digits go back to the toolbar (…), arming nothing

In the unit tests

  • numbers the families in the order the bar paints them
  • registers each digit as a real tldraw shortcut through the app overrides
  • arms the family whose digit was pressed
  • disarms when the armed family is pressed again
  • swaps family when a different digit is pressed while armed
  • does nothing with no active region and no prototype query
  • does nothing in the Dataflow lens, where the group is not rendered
  • stops answering the moment the lens leaves communication
  • claims 1, 2 and 3 while the group is on screen
  • leaves every other digit to the toolbar
  • leaves a modified digit alone — those are the toolbar and zoom shortcuts
  • claims nothing at all with the group off screen

Both gates were mutation-tested red. Deleting the isCommunicationDrawArmable guard turns the three off-screen unit checks red; deleting the claimDigits listener (CommunicationPrototypeControls.tsx:210) turns the journey red at its second check, which is how the conflict was found in the first place.

The review board

Decision surface

  • Done and proved. The three digits arm, swap and disarm; a drag after a keystroke generates the same canonical legs the button does; a digit typed into a name types; outside the lens the toolbar has its digits back. npm run check is green (tsc, 1825 vitest, 121 Python), and test:draw-hotkeys, test:communication-authoring and test:communication-focus all pass.
  • Needs you — the loan. I scoped the claim to the lens rather than turning tldraw's numbered toolbar off across the app. The alternative is one editor option (enableToolbarKeyboardShortcuts: false), which would give the digits a single meaning everywhere at the cost of a stock affordance the custom toolbar inherits. Default if you say nothing: it stays scoped.
  • Found, not fixed. npm run test:communication-prototype is red at its first check, and was already red at this branch's base commit — it reads data-projection-mode and expects 'wiring', neither of which the controls have emitted since the lens/cable split. Out of scope for this change; it needs a real update, not a rename.
  • Deliberately not done. No PEP: this is a keyboard affordance with one defensible shape, not a fork worth a numbered record. The WHY: comments at the two seams carry the reasoning.
